7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

A Nidhi Company is a type of Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) that operates in India with the primary objective of cultivating the habit of savings and thrift among its members. Registered under Section 406 of the Companies Act, 2013, a Nidhi Company is governed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and follows the Nidhi Rules, 2014. Unlike other NBFCs, a Nidhi Company is restricted to accepting deposits and lending money to its members, making it a unique financial institution.
Key Features of a Nidhi Company
A Nidhi Company can only deal with its members, meaning it cannot engage with external individuals or institutions.
The company fosters the habit of savings among its members, which promotes financial discipline.
The liability of members is limited, protecting them from financial risks beyond their contributions.
It cannot engage in chit funds, hire-purchase, leasing, or insurance businesses.
Though it falls under the NBFC category, it is exempt from Reserve Bank of India (RBI) oversight, reducing regulatory burdens.
To register a Nidhi Company in India, certain eligibility criteria must be met:
A minimum of seven members is required to start the company, with at least three acting as directors.
A minimum paid-up equity share capital of Rs. 5 lakh is necessary.
The company’s name must include the word “Nidhi Limited.”
A Nidhi Company cannot issue preference shares.
Steps to Register a Nidhi Company
Directors must have DSCs for online registration.
All directors need a DIN issued by the MCA.
The company’s name must be unique and should be approved by the MCA.

A Nidhi Company must have at least 200 members within one year of incorporation.
The ratio of Net Owned Funds to deposits should be 1:20.
The company can provide secured loans only against gold, property, or fixed deposits.
A Nidhi Company can open branches only after three years of successful operations and within the same state.
The maximum interest rate on loans cannot exceed 7.5% above the highest rate offered on deposits.
